description: §23.2.4a positive, executed — the slice's shape (single expression vs statement body) and its crossing-shadow check are decided over the slice as JavaScript TOKENS. A quote or backtick inside a regex literal (`/['x]/g`, `/["]/g`, a backtick class), a `/` inside a regex class (`/[/]+/g`), quotes inside comments, a template literal with a nested template in a `${}` hole, a chain of divisions (`12 / 3 / 2`, a single expression) and a member named `.return` are all read as what they are. Before s456 the `'` in `/['x]/g` opened a string in the compiler's character scan and hid the slice's top-level `return` (a wrong E-FOREIGN-007); a `.return(...)` member read as the `return` keyword.
rationale: §23.2.4a: a slice with no top-level `;` and no top-level `return` is a single expression (codegen injects the `return`), otherwise a statement body used verbatim; the discrimination is a syntactic scan that is string/comment/template-aware. A regex literal is a JavaScript token like a string: text inside it is not slice structure. Whether `/` starts a regex or divides is decided by the previous significant token, as the host's own lexer decides it.
